contracts.detail: POST+301 behavior changed: Before — no automatic redirect (POST completes with 301 status). After — automatic redirect to GET (GET / sent to redirect target). Confirmed by debug output: before shows only 'POST /301 -> 301 Moved Permanently' then next test, after shows 'POST /301 -> 301 Moved Permanently' then 'GET / -> 200 OK'. The side effect manifest is not stable across the patch boundary.

behavior_differences.before: POST /301 → 301 Moved Permanently → (no redirect) → next test
behavior_differences.after: POST /301 → 301 Moved Permanently → redirect → GET / → 200 OK → next test

notes: The existing redirect-test was updated in the patch to expect POST+301 redirect but is lenient on completion validation — both before and after builds pass the test suite because the test does not assert that all expected requests were received.
POST+307 (Temporary Redirect) still does NOT redirect as expected — verified by test case 23.
GET+301 normal redirect unaffected — else-if branch at line 859 still handles safe methods correctly.
Applications needing the old behavior should set SOUP_MESSAGE_NO_REDIRECT flag on SoupMessage.

conclusion.rationale: Patch line coverage 100% (7/7 executable lines covered). Behavior difference confirmed: POST+301 now automatically redirects to GET, whereas before the patch no redirect occurred. This is a genuine behavioral change — applications relying on the old behavior (no redirect for POST+301) will observe different HTTP session behavior. The change makes libsoup more standards-compliant with common HTTP client behavior (many HTTP clients redirect POST to GET on 301), but represents an incompatibility for users of the old behavior.
recommended_actions: Document the POST+301 redirect behavior change in release notes.
Note that SOUP_MESSAGE_NO_REDIRECT flag can be used by applications that need to preserve the old behavior.
Verify this change does not introduce security issues in applications that previously relied on POST+301 not being forwarded (e.g., CSRF protections).
POST+307 remains unaffected — no redirect for non-safe methods on 307 is correct per RFC 2616.
